intro: WELCOME. This is a realistic-opponent repertoire for BLACK built around the King's Indian Defence — the most ambitious answer to 1.d4 there is. Black invites White to build the big centre (d4, c4, e4), fianchettoes the dark-squared bishop to g7, strikes with ...e5, and then throws the kingside pawns forward with ...f5-f4 and ...g5-g4. It is a fighting opening: Black rarely draws quietly, and the plans are easy to remember even when the positions are sharp. Built the same way as the companion Sicilian, Queen's Gambit, Indian Defenses, English Opening, King's Indian Attack, London System and Colle System encyclopedias: main plans, common tries you'll actually meet, sharp lines, typical mistakes, every line verified move-by-move for legality. PLANNED TABLE OF CONTENTS — Chapter 1: Understanding the King's Indian (the hypermodern idea, the g7-bishop, the ...e5 break, the closed centre, the kingside storm, and when the opening does not apply). Chapter 2: The Classical Main Line (7.O-O Nc6 8.d5 Ne7 and Black's plans). Chapter 3: The Samisch and the Four Pawns Attack. Chapter 4: The Averbakh, Petrosian and Makagonov Systems. Chapter 5: The Fianchetto Variation. Chapter 6: The Exchange Variation and Early Deviations. Chapter 7: Black's Attacking Plans in Depth. Chapter 8: Traps and Tactics Compendium. Every line is completed to fifteen moves for each side with engine-verified top play, and every coach comment is preserved.
